nodes.title: Privatelink: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Privatelink. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: An application team exposes a Kubernetes service via an internal NLB in VPC-A. C?
flashcards.back: AWS PrivateLink uses a producer (VPC Endpoint Service backed by an NLB) and consumer (Interface Endpoint) model, ideal for cross-account service exposure without requiring VPC-level connectivity. This avoids CIDR-overlap concerns, does not require peering or TGW attachments, and only the specific service is exposed. Peering and TGW create network-level connectivity, which is more than what is needed. Route 53 alone does not provide private connectivity.

flashcards.front: A company wants to use Interface VPC Endpoints (PrivateLink) to access Amazon S3?
flashcards.back: AWS offers both S3 Gateway Endpoints (free, route-table based, in-VPC only) and S3 Interface Endpoints (PrivateLink, charged per hour + data processed, support access from on-premises and cross-VPC/account). Many architectures use both. Interface Endpoints for S3 are globally available, not GovCloud-only. and/or Gateway Endpoints for in-VPC access at no additional charge

flashcards.front: A company wants to enforce that all VPC endpoints created in member accounts mus?
flashcards.back: Organization-wide enforcement of VPC endpoint policies is achieved by combining SCPs (deny creation of non-compliant endpoints), Config rules (detect non-compliant endpoints), and automated remediation (SSM / Lambda). AWS Firewall Manager focuses on SG/WAF/NFW/DNS Firewall policies, not generic endpoint policies. RAM is sharing, not policy enforcement. Shield is DDoS-focused.

flashcards.front: A company has a private ALB in a VPC and wants to expose it to customers over Pr?
flashcards.back: VPC Endpoint Services (PrivateLink provider side) can be backed by NLBs or GWLBs. To expose an ALB via PrivateLink, you create an NLB with ALB-type target (supported since 2021), then create the VPC Endpoint Service on that NLB. Consumers use Interface Endpoints. You cannot create an endpoint service directly from an ALB. API Gateway is unrelated.

nodes.title: Cloudfront: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Cloudfront. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: A media streaming company uses CloudFront with an S3 origin serving premium cont?
flashcards.back: Origin Access Control (OAC) is the modern replacement for OAI, supporting SigV4 and SSE-KMS. CloudFront signed URLs are the standard short-lived token mechanism. CloudFront geo restriction (or WAF geo match rule) blocks countries. Shield Advanced is for DDoS, not geo-blocking. S3 pre-signed URLs would expose the bucket directly. use CloudFront signed URLs for short-lived tokens, and apply CloudFront geo restriction (or AWS WAF geo match rule) to block restricted countries

flashcards.front: A company has an ALB behind CloudFront and needs to ensure CloudFront viewers ca?
flashcards.back: The recommended patterns are either (1) using the AWS Managed Prefix List for CloudFront (com.amazonaws.global.cloudfront.origin-facing) in the ALB security group, or (2) using a custom header on CloudFront and a WAF rule on the ALB validating it. Both prevent direct access. Lambda maintaining IP lists is outdated. GWLB is not suitable. A private ALB with no NAT would not be reachable from CloudFront either.

flashcards.front: A company uses CloudFront in front of multiple origins and wants to selectively ?
flashcards.back: CloudFront Functions run at all 600+ edge locations, have sub-millisecond startup, cost fraction vs Lambda@Edge, and are designed for lightweight header manipulation, URL rewrites, and simple auth checks. Lambda@Edge works but has higher latency, cost, and runs only at regional edge caches. WAF response headers are for WAF actions, not general manipulation. Origin Shield is a regional cache layer, not transformation.

flashcards.front: A company has a CloudFront distribution serving content from multiple origins gl?
flashcards.back: CloudFront Origin Shield is an additional centralized cache layer that consolidates requests from all edge locations, dramatically reducing origin load and improving cache hit ratios. Higher TTLs help but cannot always be used. CloudFront Functions and Lambda@Edge are for transformations, not cache consolidation.

nodes.title: Mixed Topics: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Mixed Topics. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: A financial services company needs a hybrid DNS architecture where on-premises D?
flashcards.back: Route 53 Resolver endpoints solve hybrid DNS. Inbound endpoints receive DNS queries from on-premises (for AWS private zones), while outbound endpoints forward DNS queries from AWS to on-premises resolvers using forwarding rules tied to domain names. This is the AWS-recommended hybrid DNS pattern. DHCP Option Sets with custom DNS servers work but require you to manage BIND yourself. Public hosted zones are not appropriate for internal names.

flashcards.front: A company uses Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall to block requests to known malicio?
flashcards.back: Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall supports AWS Managed Domain Lists such as malware and botnet C&C lists that are continuously updated. You associate them into a rule group with BLOCK action and associate the rule group with VPCs. GuardDuty detects but does not directly block DNS. Manual lists require ongoing maintenance. flashcards.front: A regulated customer requires all DNS traffic within their VPCs to go through th?
flashcards.back: A forwarding rule with domain name '.' (root) configured on an outbound endpoint forwards all DNS queries to on-premises targets. The rule must be associated with the relevant VPCs. Disabling VPC DNS would break internal AWS resolution. Inbound endpoints are for on-prem to AWS queries. Private hosted zones do not provide forwarding.

flashcards.front: A global company uses Route 53 with latency-based routing and health checks for ?
flashcards.back: Latency-based routing returns the record with the lowest latency among healthy records. If Singapore users get routed to eu-west-1, the ap-southeast-1 record is likely unhealthy (failing health check), missing, or misconfigured. Verify health check status and that the record is properly tagged with Region=ap-southeast-1. Latency routing is not region-restricted. the health check is failing, or the record is not associated with the correct region/latency base; verify the health check status and record configuration
